dlcservice: Unify into simple logic for exposed APIs Dlcservice exposes 3 main APIs: - Install - Uninstall - GetInstall Within this CL, we try and break those APIs into calling helpers for high level understanding that is simple. Sequence of events that should happen for each API: - Install: CreateDlc - Uninstall: UnmountDlc, DeleteDlc - GetInstall: Just return the installed DLC(s). Currently these APIs are dependent on the fact that |LoadDlcModuleImages()| will always fully succeed and give rise to a |installed_dlc_modules_| that is completely valid. |OnStatusUpdateAdvancedSignal()| will only return a single type of error as the user should not care whether |ImageLoader| was the reason for the failure, but the mounting itself failed. This will require improvements to |MountDlc()|. Note: No breakage of old unittests. BUG=none TEST=FEATURES="test" emerge-$BOARD dlcservice TEST=tast run $TEST_IP platform.DLCService Change-Id: I62e2e1b4df8b310fc08eb215e0874f94e21ed2fa Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1730169 Tested-by: Jae Hoon Kim <kimjae@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Jae Hoon Kim <kimjae@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Xiaochu Liu <xiaochu@chromium.org>

dlcservice: Maintain cache state of dlc roots Dlcservice will maintain the dlc roots alongside the installed DLC(s). During |LoadDlcModuleImages()|, it is already the case that if a mounting fails then the failed DLC will not end up in |installed_dlc_modules_|, so |LoadDlcModuleImages()| will only add to the |installed_dlc_modules_| DLC(s) that are installed with mount. During |Install()|, no change is made to |installed_dlc_modules_|. During |Uninstall()|, we only remove from |installed_dlc_modules_| if unmounting and deleting both succeed (neither unmount nor delete should ever fail, but in the case that they do, it will lead dlcservice into an unstable state). Deleting al already deleted file or directory returns true and will not fail, which desired behavior. During |OnStatusUpdateAdvancedSignal()| most of the work happens. Dlcservice goes through the DLC(s) that finished installing and need to be mounted. Only when all the `to be` installed DLC(s) are mounted, do they go into the |installed_dlc_modules_| with there corresponding dlc roots. cryptohome: Add new commandline features for cryptohome commandline tool. To add new data restore key, simply type: cryptohome --action=add_data_restore_key --user=your_user_name Then type in your password, wait for a few second, then the hex string of data restore key will be displayed if authenticated. To build authentication, testers can use switch "--restore_key_in_hex" to provide data restore key in HexString, for instance if testers type: cryptohome --action=check_key_ex --user=your_user_name --restore_key_in_hex=0123456789ABCDEF Cryptohome will use restore key in AuthorizationRequest and check if it can be authenticated. To mass remove keys, users need to provide exempt key labels. Every other keyset whose label is not in exempt_key_labels will be removed. For instance, if users have four keysets which are labeled as "l1", "l2", "l3" and "l4", say if they want to delete l1 and l2 and keep l3 and l4, they should type: cryptohome --action=mass_remove_keys --user=your_user_name --exempt_key_labels=l3,l4 After authenticated, l1 and l2 will be removed. network_WiFi_LinkMonitorFailure: don't fail upon lack of disconnect This test is testing to ensure (a) Shill's link monitor detects a link failure (e.g., failing ARP requests) within a certain timeout and (b) the rest of the stack (driver, wpa_supplicant) responds appropriately when Shill requests a WiFi Reattach() Reattach() is just a "Reassociation attempt": https://w1.fi/wpa_supplicant/devel/dbus.html#dbus_interface which traditionally resulted in a disconnect/reconnect, but is now widened such that some drivers support the reassociation attempt directly, and therefore do not yield any disconnect. See https://crbug.com/990012#c4 for some more information about this. Anyway, the result is the 'iw event' only shows the "connected" event, with no disconnect in the meantime. This was confirmed in a WiFi sniffer packet capture. Since this behavior doesn't really violate (b), we should loosen this restriction, and avoid failing the test just because we didn't see a disconnect. A Reassociation should be as good as a Deauth/Reassociation in terms of "un-sticking" the driver. BUG=chromium:990012 TEST=run it on veyron_minnie-kernelnext Change-Id: Iddc454cbfde00aa23e60de1cfdf9d956e79d2f9a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1737468 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Neeraj Poojary <npoojary@chromium.org>

net-print/ippusbxd: Adding exponential backoff for print read requests Initiating read requests uses an asynchronous callback system where requests are sent to the printer and then a callback will fire with the printer's response. If the printer currently has no data to service the read request then it responds with a 0-byte message. This system lead to ippusbxd spamming the printer continuously with read requests that came back with empty responses. This change introduces exponential backoff so that if an empty response is received from the printer, ippusbxd will wait for increasingly long periods before issuing another request. This change significantly reduces syslog spam, and should result in faster communication with the printer. BUG=None TEST=Passes printer.PrintIPPUSB tast test on asuka device Change-Id: I79352f3f3b35d0bd3eba140c1af1a9a3b152ca89 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1739922 Tested-by: David Valleau <valleau@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: David Valleau <valleau@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Kau <skau@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kalvin Lee <kdlee@chromium.org>

dlcservice: Install completion determined from DBus signal When update_engine signals its listeners of a status update, dlcservice is one of those listeners. Previously, dlcservice determined that update engine was done installing DLC(s) based off that fact that dlcservice held onto the DLC(s) it sent over to update_engine and that update_engine sent a status with operation IDLE. Now, a more solidified method of letting update_engine, who knows whether an install or update is in progress, indicate this field through `is_install` within |update_engine::StatusResult| is used by dlcservice to determined an install completion. servo: micro + ccd on same instance (round 2). Note: This is a temporay hack as go/servoarch will provide the same functionality, however in this case we need this double feature earlier. Expect this to be gone with servoarch with the rest of postinit. This change adds a new layer to postinit to allow for servo micro and ccd on the same servo instance iff both micro and ccd are enumerated and on the same v4 hub. In that case, the servo micro is the main device, and all controls route to it. However, ccd backed controls are also available behind the ccd_cr50. prefix. This is off by default and can be enabled by having --allow-dual-v4 in the cmdline. To that effect the change adds that to the upstart script used in the lab. E.g. dut-control cr50_devid // used servo micro to query the devid dut-control ccd_cr50.cr50_devid // uses ccd to query the devid BUG=None TEST=manual testing > passes labstation validation > EC/AP/Cr50 console through micro work > Cr50 console through ccd works sudo servod -b atlas --allow-dual-v4 2019-07-15 09:22:15,736 - ServoDeviceWatchdog - INFO - Watchdog setup for devices: set([(6353, 20507, 'C1709150019'), (6353, 20500, u'16000062-935CD754'), (6353, 20506, u'SNCQ00098')]) // showing both micro and ccd got pulled in. sudo servod -b atlas 2019-07-15 09:21:47,961 - ServoDeviceWatchdog - INFO - Watchdog setup for devices: set([(6353, 20507, 'C1709150019'), (6353, 20506, u'SNCQ00098')]) // showing only micro got pulled in. TEST=sudo servod -b atlas // with v4 + micro >> comes up fine TEST=sudo servod -b atlas --allow-dual-v4 // with v4 + micro >> comes up fine, dual role ignored TEST=sudo servod -b atlas // with v4 + ccd >> comes up fine TEST=sudo servod -b atlas --allow-dual-v4 // with v4 + ccd >> comes up fine, dual role ignored TEST=sudo servod -b atlas // with v4 + micro + ccd >> comes up fine TEST=sudo servod -b atlas --allow-dual-v4 // with v4 + micro + ccd >> comes up fine, dual role honored Change-Id: I56aa10128565f6198f2c4c70ed09dd544b94c3a2 Signed-off-by: Ruben Rodriguez Buchillon <coconutruben@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1737187 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mary Ruthven <mruthven@chromium.org>
